content.text: bisphosphonates inhibit osteoclasts; usually the drugs of choice for cancer-associated hypercalcemia; zoledronic acid 4 mg IV once lowers Ca for an average of > 40 days; pamidronate 60 to 90 mg IV once, repeated only after 7 days; lowers Ca for ≤ 2 wks; repeated IV bisphosphonates (bone mets, myeloma) are linked to ONJ; renal toxicity reported w zoledronic acid; oral bisphosphonates can maintain normal Ca but aren't generally used acutely; denosumab: cancer-associated hypercalcemia not responding to bisphosphonates; 120 mg SC every 4 wks + extra doses on days 8 and 15 of the first month; give Ca and vitamin D prn to avert hypocalcemia; calcitonin (salmon) 4 to 8 IU/kg SC every 12 h; can ↓Ca by 1 to 2 mg/dL within a few hours; in cancer-associated hypercalcemia, limited by short action w tachyphylaxis (often after ~48 h) and no response in ≥ 40%. salmon calcitonin + prednisone may control Ca for months in some cancer pts.

CI: hypocalcemia (must be corrected b4 starting Xgeva). CI: known clinically significant hypersensitivity to Xgeva or denosumab products. Can cause severe symptomatic hypocalcemia w/ fatal cases; correct hypocalcemia b4 starting; monitor Ca esp in the first wks; adequately supplement all pts w/ Ca and vitamin D. ↑ risk of hypocalcemia w/ increasing renal dysfunction, most commonly severe dysfunction (CrCl less than 30 mL/min and/or on dialysis), and w/ inadequate/no Ca supplementation. Hypersensitivity reactions incl anaphylaxis may occur; discontinue permanently if a clinically significant reaction occurs. ONJ reported; perform an oral exam b4 starting; monitor for symptoms; ⍉ invasive dental procedures during tx. Atypical femoral fracture: evaluate pts w/ thigh or groin pain to rule out a femoral fracture. Multiple vertebral fractures reported after discontinuation; when Xgeva is stopped, evaluate the pt's risk for vertebral fractures. Hypercalcemia requiring hospitalization and complicated by acute renal injury reported after treatment discontinuation in pts w/ giant cell tumor of bone and growing skeletons. May cause fetal harm; advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during therapy and for at least 5 mo after the last dose. Pts receiving Xgeva should ⍉ receive other denosumab products concomitantly.

CI: hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon or any of the excipients (reactions incl anaphylaxis w/ death, bronchospasm, and swelling of the tongue or throat). Serious hypersensitivity reactions incl fatal anaphylaxis reported; consider skin testing b4 treatment in pts w/ suspected hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon. Hypocalcemia w/ tetany (muscle cramps, twitching) and seizure activity reported; hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy. Meta-analysis of 21 trials suggests an ↑ risk of overall malignancies in calcitonin salmon-treated pts. Circulating antibodies to calcitonin salmon may develop and may cause loss of response to treatment. Use for Paget's dz or postmenopausal osteoporosis is recommended w/ an adequate intake of Ca and vitamin D. Concomitant lithium may ↓ plasma lithium concentrations (↑ urinary clearance); lithium dose may require adjustment. OD: hypocalcemic tetany could occur; keep parenteral calcium available for treatment. Most common adverse reactions: nausea w/ or w/o vomiting (10%), injection site inflammation (10%), and flushing of the face or hands (2% to 5%). Due to the possible association between malignancy and calcitonin salmon use, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated periodically.
